fit.gap_handling_summary: The outputs present the core React/TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL and sensitive-document experience accurately, without inventing healthcare, accessibility or testing credentials. Security-sensitive fintech work is a useful adjacent qualification, but it does not establish OWASP, GDPR or audit experience. Accessibility, automated testing and responsive-web fundamentals remain major unaddressed evidence gaps; mobile-app work does not establish low-end mobile-web performance expertise.

artefacts: The BankID project contains two consecutive bullets describing essentially the same implementation.
“English: Proficiency level not specified” reads like an unresolved drafting note rather than finished application content.
issues: Only a first name is supplied; there is no email, telephone number or usable portfolio/GitHub URL. The source material does not provide these details, so they should be requested rather than invented.
TypeORM and Prisma are ORMs, not databases; the skills category should distinguish them from PostgreSQL.
Achievements and project descriptions are repeated across the summary, employment section and project section.
The Nordkust Media role has no description despite the source establishing newspaper-site work.
Selected projects are neither reverse chronological nor clearly ordered around the most relevant recent work.

reasons: The PDF extracts in a sensible single-column order with intact words and standard headings.
The principal stack and sufficient professional tenure are explicit.
Fintech, provider-SDK integration and measured A/B testing provide relevant contextual matches.
Core screening areas—accessibility, automated testing and Git workflows—are not established. GitHub publication alone does not prove a professional Git workflow.
English is mentioned but fluency is explicitly left unconfirmed.
Missing contact information weakens the completeness of the application record.

issues: The company-specific paragraph mostly references principles rather than a concrete product or recent patient-experience initiative.
It does not explicitly express willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements or address the role's accessibility and testing emphasis.
“My recent work” refers to projects dated 2022 and 2023; less time-sensitive wording would be sharper in a 2026 application.
The motivation and team-lead experience share one paragraph, slightly diluting the company-focused argument.
strengths: Names Verdane Care, the exact role and the Patient Experience team.
Uses a concrete conversion improvement and explains relevant implementation details.
Connects sensitive fintech workflows to patient-facing software without claiming healthcare or GDPR expertise.
Accurately describes temporary acting leadership rather than promoting it into a permanent title.
Avoids the earlier letter's obsolete agency-to-product transition and lack of NestJS experience.
Concise, professional and comfortably within one page.

spacing_issues: The Ferry Ticket Mobile App heading is stranded at the bottom of CV page 1, with all its bullets on page 2.
CV page 1 is relatively dense while page 2 has substantial unused lower-page space.
issues: The measurements report no geometric problems, but the images reveal a poor project-heading page break.
The letter has ample lower-page whitespace, which is acceptable for a short letter rather than evidence of overflow or missing content.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “English: Proficiency level not specified” is administrative wording, not polished candidate-facing CV language.
“Delivered a new onboarding identity step…” followed immediately by “Implemented a Swedish BankID identity-verification flow…” is conspicuously repetitive.

notes_facts_used: Twelve years of professional experience counted from 2014.
Frontend strength, consistent with the earlier letter's React/TypeScript confidence.
Maintenance of one GraphQL BFF using Apollo Server, without claiming deep expertise.
Four-month acting-team-lead assignment in 2024, including one-to-ones and sprint planning.

parsed.summary: The application accurately presents a strong React/TypeScript, NestJS and PostgreSQL background, supported by measurable conversion results and relevant sensitive-data work. The cover letter is concise, company-specific and free of stale claims from the earlier application. The CV needs contact details, removal of duplicate content, a finished language section and a corrected project page break. Accessibility, automated testing, Git workflows and health-data privacy remain important unverified requirements rather than qualifications the outputs can legitimately claim.
